_comment: The Neutralino release this build123d Studio is built against, and the
SHA-256 of every binary taken from it. scripts/ensure-neutralino.mjs checks
bin/ against these before any build and fetches the release when something
is missing or does not match; nothing is ever executed unverified.
These binaries become the application executable in every package. They used
to be downloaded by a `postinstall: neu update` hook on every yarn install,
with no checksum and no signature - the least verified input to the shipped
product, while the uv binary beside it was checked against a committed
digest.
What this proves and what it does not: the digests were taken from the
official release zip, whose own SHA-256 matched the digest published by the
GitHub releases API - a different origin from the asset bytes, so a tampered
or intercepted download is caught. It cannot prove the release itself is
honest. Neutralino publishes no build provenance: its attestations API
returns 404 and its release workflow has no attest-build-provenance step
(checked 2026-07-28). uv can be verified with `gh attestation verify`; this
cannot.
To move the pin: node scripts/ensure-neutralino.mjs --update <version>
Do not edit the digests by hand.
Only the binaries the packaging targets use are listed. The release also
ships mac_universal and linux_armhf; nothing builds for them. This list and
TARGETS in scripts/package.mjs have to agree.
